name: accelerate
description: A pattern of numbers that speed up (or slow down) samples while they play. Currently only supported by osc / superdirt.

name: add
description: Assumes a pattern of numbers. Adds the given number to each item in the pattern.

name: addVoicings
description: Adds a new custom voicing dictionary.

params.name: dictionary
params.description: maps chord symbol to possible voicings

name: adsr
description: ADSR envelope: Combination of Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Release.

name: allTransforms
description:
Applies a function to all the running patterns. Note that the patterns are groups together into a single stack before the function is applied. This is probably what you want, but see each for
a version that applies the function to each pattern separately.
$: sound("bd - cp sd")
$: sound("hh*8")
all(fast("<2 3>"))

$: sound("bd - cp sd")
$: sound("hh*8")
all(x => x.pianoroll())

name: almostAlways
description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.9, fn)

name: almostNever
description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.1, fn)

name: always
description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(1, fn) (always calls fn)

name: amp
description: Like gain, but linear.

name: analyzeColonContext
description: Determine if position is in colon syntax context

name: appBoth
description:
When this method is called on a pattern of functions, it matches its haps
with those in the given pattern of values.  A new pattern is returned, with
each matching value applied to the corresponding function.
In this _appBoth variant, where timespans of the function and value haps
are not the same but do intersect, the resulting hap has a timespan of the
intersection. This applies to both the part and the whole timespan.

name: appLeft
description:
As with appBoth, but the whole timespan is not the intersection,
but the timespan from the function of patterns that this method is called
on. In practice, this means that the pattern structure, including onsets,
are preserved from the pattern of functions (often referred to as the left
hand or inner pattern).

name: apply
description: Like layer, but with a single function:

name: appRight
description:
As with appLeft, but whole timespans are instead taken from the
pattern of values, i.e. structure is preserved from the right hand/outer
pattern.

name: appWhole
description:
Assumes 'this' is a pattern of functions, and given a function to
resolve wholes, applies a given pattern of values to that
pattern of functions.

name: arp
description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

name: arpWith
description: Selects indices in in stacked notes.

name: arrange
description:
Allows to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles.
Takes a variable number of arrays with two elements specifying the number of cycles and the pattern to use.

name: as
description: Sets properties in a batch.

params.name: mapping
params.description: the control names that are set

name: asym
description: Asymmetrical diode distortion

name: attack
description: Amplitude envelope attack time: Specifies how long it takes for the sound to reach its peak value, relative to the onset.

name: autoFormatOnSave
description: Auto-format on save functionality

name: bank
description: Select the sound bank to use. To be used together with s. The bank name (+ "_") will be prepended to the value of s.
examples: s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").bank('RolandTR909') // = s("RolandTR909_bd RolandTR909_sd")

name: beat
description:
creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle
especially useful for creating rhythms

name: begin
description: A pattern of numbers from 0 to 1. Skips the beginning of each sample, e.g. 0.25 to cut off the first quarter from each sample.

params.name: amount
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

name: berlin
description:
Generates a continuous pattern of [berlin noise](conceived by Jame Coyne and Jade Rowland as a joke but turned out to be surprisingly cool and useful,
like perlin noise but with sawtooth waves), in the range 0..1.

name: binary
description: Creates a pattern from a binary number.

params.name: n
params.description: input number to convert to binary

name: binaryN
description: Creates a pattern from a binary number, padded to n bits long.

params.name: n
params.description: input number to convert to binary

name: bite
description:
Splits a pattern into the given number of slices, and plays them according to a pattern of slice numbers.
Similar to slice, but slices up patterns rather than sound samples.

name: bpattack
description: Sets the attack duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

params.name: attack
params.description: time of the bandpass filter envelope

name: bpdecay
description: Sets the decay duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

params.name: decay
params.description: time of the bandpass filter envelope

name: bpenv
description: Sets the bandpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.description: depth of the bandpass filter envelope between 0 and n

name: bpf
description:
Sets the center frequency of the band-pass filter. When using mininotation, you
can also optionally supply the 'bpq' parameter separated by ':'.

name: bpq
description: Sets the band-pass q-factor (resonance).

name: bprelease
description: Sets the release time for the bandpass filter envelope.

params.name: release
params.description: time of the bandpass filter envelope

name: bpsustain
description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the bandpass filter envelope.

params.name: sustain
params.description: amplitude of the bandpass filter envelope

name: brak
description:
Returns a new pattern where every other cycle is played once, twice as
fast, and offset in time by one quarter of a cycle. Creates a kind of
breakbeat feel.

name: brand
description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random)

name: brandBy
description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random), with a probability for the value being 1

name: byteBeatExpression
description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

name: byteBeatStartTime
description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

name: calculateScore
description: Calculate match score for ranking

name: cat
description: The given items are concatenated, where each one takes one cycle.

name: ccn
description: MIDI control number: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: ccv
description: MIDI control value: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: ceil
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical ceiling. E.g. 3.2 replaced with 4, and -4.2
replaced with -4.

name: channel
description: Choose the channel the pattern is sent to in superdirt

name: channels
description: Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

name: chebyshev
description: Distortion via Chebyshev polynomials

name: choose
description: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements.

name: choose2
description:
As with choose, but the pattern that this method is called on should be
in the range -1 .. 1

name: chooseCycles
description: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle.

name: chooseInWith
description:
As with {chooseWith}, but the structure comes from the chosen values, rather
than the pattern you're using to choose with.

name: chooseWith
description:
Choose from the list of values (or patterns of values) using the given
pattern of numbers, which should be in the range of 0..1

name: chop
description:
Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'.
It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.
examples:
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
 .chop(4)
 .rev() // reverse order of chops
 .loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles

name: chorus
description: mix control for the chorus effect

name: chunk
description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

name: chunkBack
description: Like chunk, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

name: chunkBackInto
description: Like chunkInto, but moves backwards through the chunks.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

name: chunkInto
description: Like chunk, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
  .bank("tr909")

name: clip
description: Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

name: coarse
description: Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

params.name: factor
params.description: 1 for original 2 for half, 3 for a third and so on.

name: color
description: Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

name: compress
description: Compress each cycle into the given timespan, leaving a gap
examples:
cat(
  s("bd sd").compress(.25,.75),
  s("~ bd sd ~")
)

name: compressor
description:
Dynamics Compressor. The params are compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release")
More info here

name: contract
description:
Experimental
Contracts the step size of the pattern by the given factor. See also expand.

name: control
description: MIDI control: Sends a MIDI control change message.

name: cosine
description: A cosine signal between 0 and 1.

name: cosine2
description: A cosine signal between -1 and 1 (like cosine, but bipolar).

name: cpm
description: Plays the pattern at the given cycles per minute.

name: createMockContext
description:
Create a mock CodeMirror autocomplete context.
The key method is matchBefore(regex) which tests the text before the cursor
against a regex and returns { text, from, to } if it matches, or null.

params.name: fullText
params.description: The full text in the editor

name: crush
description: Bit crusher effect.

params.name: depth
params.description: between 1 (for drastic reduction in bit-depth) to 16 (for barely no reduction).

name: csoundm
description:
Sends notes to Csound for rendering with MIDI semantics. The hap value is
translated to these Csound pfields:
p1 -- Csound instrument either as a number (1-based, can be a fraction),
or as a string name.
p2 -- time in beats (usually seconds) from start of performance.
p3 -- duration in beats (usually seconds).
p4 -- MIDI key number (as a real number, not an integer but in [0, 127].
p5 -- MIDI velocity (as a real number, not an integer but in [0, 127].
p6 -- Strudel controls, as a string.

name: cubic
description: Cubic polynomial distortion

name: cut
description: In the style of classic drum-machines, cut will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

name: decay
description:
Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level.
Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

name: defragmentHaps
description:
Combines adjacent haps with the same value and whole.  Only
intended for use in tests.

name: degrade
description: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .degradeBy(0.5)

name: degradeBy
description:
Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount.
0 = 0% chance of removal
1 = 100% chance of removal

name: delay
description:
Sets the level of the delay signal.
When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter,
separated by ':'.

name: delayfeedback
description:
Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay.
Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

name: delayspeed
description: Sets the time of the delay effect.

params.name: delayspeed
params.description: controls the pitch of the delay feedback

name: delaysync
description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

name: density
description: Noise crackle density

name: detectPositionType
description: Detect current position type in pattern

name: detune
description: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

name: diode
description: Diode-emulating distortion

name: discreteOnly
description:
Returns a new pattern, with 'continuous' haps (those without 'whole'
timespans) removed from query results.

name: distort
description:
Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud.
Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type.
Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

name: distorttype
description: Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.
examples:
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
  .penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
  .distort(rand.range(1, 8))
  .distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")

name: distortvol
description: Postgain for waveshaping distortion.

name: div
description: Divides each number by the given factor.

name: djf
description: DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

params.name: cutoff
params.description: below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter

name: drawLine
description:
Intended for a debugging, drawLine renders the pattern as a string, where each character represents the same time span.
Should only be used with single characters as values, otherwise the character slots will be messed up.
Character legend:

"|" cycle separator
"-" hold previous value
"." silence

name: drive
description: Filter overdrive for supported filter types
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")

name: drop
description:
Experimental
Drops the given number of steps from a pattern.
A positive number will drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: dry
description: Set dryness of reverb. See room and size for more information about reverb.

name: duckattack
description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.
Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

name: duckdepth
description:
The amount of ducking applied to target orbit
Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckdepth("0.3:0.1").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").

name: duckonset
description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume.
Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.
Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckonset("0:0.003").
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. duckorbit("2:3").
examples:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

name: duckorbit
description:
Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.
Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. duckorbit("2:3")

name: duration
description: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

name: each
description:
Applies a function to each of the running patterns separately. This is intended for future use with upcoming 'stepwise' features. See all for a version that applies the function to all the patterns stacked together into a single pattern.
$: sound("bd - cp sd")
$: sound("hh*8")
each(fast("<2 3>"))

name: early
description: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to nudge left

name: echo
description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

name: echoWith
description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

name: end
description: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

params.name: length
params.description: 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..

name: euclid
description:
Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm.
Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common
divisor of two numbers.  They were described in 2004 by Godfried
Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist.  Euclidean rhythms are
really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can
describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

name: euclidish
description:
A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting
rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example
sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0) would be the same as
sound("bd").euclid(3,8), and sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1) would be the
same as sound("bd bd bd"). sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5) would have a
groove somewhere between.
Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

params.name: groove
params.description: exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)

name: euclidLegato
description:
Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

name: euclidLegatoRot
description:
Similar to euclid, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating'
the resulting sequence

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

name: euclidRot
description: Like euclid, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.

params.name: steps
params.description: the number of steps to fill

examples:
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)

name: every
description: An alias for firstOf

name: expand
description:
Experimental
Expands the step size of the pattern by the given factor.

name: extend
description:
Experimental
extend is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count
accordingly. So stepcat("a b".extend(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas
stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").extend(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

name: fanchor
description: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
examples:
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

name: fast
description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

name: fastChunk
description:
Like chunk, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated
for each set of chunks.

name: fastGap
description: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

name: filter
description: Filters haps using the given function

name: filterHaps
description: Returns a new Pattern, which only returns haps that meet the given test.

params.name: hap_test
params.description: a function which returns false for haps to be removed from the pattern

name: filterValues
description:
As with filterHaps, but the function is applied to values
inside haps.

name: filterWhen
description: Filters haps by their begin time

name: findSeparators
description: Identify pattern separators and boundaries

name: firstCycle
description:
Queries the pattern for the first cycle, returning Haps. Mainly of use when
debugging a pattern.

params.name: with_context
params.description:
set to true, otherwise the context field
will be stripped from the resulting haps.

name: firstCycleValues
description: Accessor for a list of values returned by querying the first cycle.

name: firstOf
description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

name: fit
description:
Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks.
Similar to loopAt.

name: floor
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical floor. E.g. 3.7 replaced with to 3, and -4.2
replaced with -5.

name: fm
description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth.
Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()

name: fmap
description: see withValue

name: fmattack
description: Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()

name: fmdecay
description: Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()

name: fmenv
description: Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.2)
.fmsustain(0)
.fmenv("<exp lin>")
._scope()

name: fmh
description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio.
Controls the timbre of the sound.
Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural,
while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")
._scope()

name: fmsustain
description: Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()

name: fmwave
description: Waveform of the fm modulator

name: focus
description: Similar to compress, but doesn't leave gaps, and the 'focus' can be bigger than a cycle

name: fold
description: Wavefolding distortion

name: formatCode
description: Formats code using Prettier

name: formatCommand
description: Format command that formats the entire document or selection

name: formatEngine
description:
Prettier extension for CodeMirror
Provides formatting commands and keyboard shortcuts

name: formatSelection
description: Formats a selection of code

name: formatStrudelCode
description: Formats Strudel code with basic formatting while preserving DSL syntax

name: freq
description: Set frequency of sound.

params.name: frequency
params.description: in Hz. the audible range is between 20 and 20000 Hz

name: fromBipolar
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the unipolar range 0 .. 1

name: fscope
description: Renders an oscilloscope for the frequency domain of the audio signal.

params.name: color
params.description: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.description: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

params.name: lean
params.description: y-axis alignment where 0 = top and 1 = bottom

name: ftype
description: Sets the filter type. The ladder filter is more aggressive. More types might be added in the future.
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)

note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2)
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(200).fanchor(0)
.lpenv(3).lpq(1)
.ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")

name: gain
description: Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

name: gap
description: Does absolutely nothing, but with a given metrical 'steps'

name: getCurrentElement
description: Find the current pattern element at position

name: getCurrentSettings
description: Gets current settings from the settings store

name: getPrettierConfig
description: Gets or creates a cached Prettier configuration

name: grow
description:
Experimental
Progressively grows the pattern by 'n' steps until the full pattern is played, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :),
that number of times.
A positive number will progressively grow steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: hard
description: Hard-clipping distortion

name: hideLoadingIndicator
description: Hides the loading indicator

name: hpattack
description: Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: attack
params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

name: hpdecay
description: Sets the decay duration for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: decay
params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

name: hpenv
description: Sets the highpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.description: depth of the highpass filter envelope between 0 and n

name: hpf
description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the high-pass filter.
When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: hpq
description: Controls the high-pass q-value.

name: hprelease
description: Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: release
params.description: time of the highpass filter envelope

name: hpsustain
description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

params.name: sustain
params.description: amplitude of the highpass filter envelope

name: hurry
description: Both speeds up the pattern (like 'fast') and the sample playback (like 'speed').

name: hush
description: Silences a pattern.

name: inhabit
description:
Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name).
Similar to pick, but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.

name: inhabitmod
description:
The same as inhabit, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.
For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the
second one.

name: inside
description: Carries out an operation 'inside' a cycle.

name: into
description:
Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern.
True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the
source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be
applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern
to be played unchanged.

name: invert
description: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

name: irand
description: A continuous pattern of random integers, between 0 and n-1.
examples:
// randomly select scale notes from 0 - 7 (= C to C)
n(irand(8)).struct("x x*2 x x*3").scale("C:minor")

name: irbegin
description: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

name: iresponse
description: Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

params.name: sample
params.description: to use as an impulse response

name: irspeed
description: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

name: isAfterSeparator
description: Check if position is after a pattern separator

name: isaw
description: A sawtooth signal between 1 and 0 (like saw, but flipped).

name: isaw2
description: A sawtooth signal between 1 and -1 (like saw2, but flipped).

name: isStrudelCode
description: Detects if code contains Strudel-specific syntax

name: iter
description: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

name: iterBack
description: Like iter, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

name: itri
description: An inverted triangle signal between 1 and 0 (like tri, but flipped).

name: itri2
description: An inverted triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like itri, but bipolar).

name: jux
description: The jux function creates strange stereo effects, by applying a function to a pattern, but only in the right-hand channel.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").jux(iter(4))

name: juxBy
description: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

name: keyDown
description:
returns true when a key or array of keys is held
Key name reference

name: label
description: Sets the displayed text for an event on the pianoroll

name: lastOf
description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the last cycle.

name: late
description: Nudge a pattern to start later in time. Equivalent of Tidal's ~> operator

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to nudge right

name: layer
description: Layers the result of the given function(s). Like superimpose, but without the original pattern:

name: leslie
description: Emulation of a Leslie speaker: speakers rotating in a wooden amplified cabinet.

name: linger
description: Selects the given fraction of the pattern and repeats that part to fill the remainder of the cycle.

name: lock
description: Specifies whether delaytime is calculated relative to cps.

params.name: enable
params.description: When set to 1, delaytime is a direct multiple of a cycle.

name: log
description: Writes the content of the current event to the console (visible in the side menu).

name: logFormattingError
description: Logs formatting errors with privacy protection

name: logValues
description:
A simplified version of log which writes all "values" (various configurable parameters)
within the event to the console (visible in the side menu).

name: loop
description:
Loops the sample.
Note that the tempo of the loop is not synced with the cycle tempo.
To change the loop region, use loopBegin / loopEnd.

name: loopAt
description: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles by changing the speed.

name: loopAtCps
description:
Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles and cps value, by
changing the speed. Please note that at some point cps will be
given by a global clock and this function will be
deprecated/removed.

name: loopBegin
description:
Begin to loop at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end).
Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and before loopEnd!
Note: Samples starting with wt_ will automatically loop! (wt = wavetable)

params.name: time
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

name: loopEnd
description:
End the looping section at a specific point in the sample (inbetween begin and end).
Note that the loop point must be inbetween begin and end, and after loopBegin!

params.name: time
params.description: between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample

name: lpattack
description: Sets the attack duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpdecay
description: Sets the decay duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpenv
description: Sets the lowpass filter envelope modulation depth.

params.name: modulation
params.description: depth of the lowpass filter envelope between 0 and n

name: lpf
description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter.
When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'lpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: lpq
description: Controls the low-pass q-value.

name: lprelease
description: Sets the release time for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: lpsustain
description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the lowpass filter envelope.

params.name: sustain
params.description: amplitude of the lowpass filter envelope

name: lrate
description: Rate of modulation / rotation for leslie effect

name: lsize
description: Physical size of the cabinet in meters. Be careful, it might be slightly larger than your computer. Affects the Doppler amount (pitch warble)

name: markcss
description: Overrides the css of highlighted events. Make sure to use single quotes!

name: mask
description: Returns silence when mask is 0 or "~"

name: match
description: Filter samples by case-insensitive matching

name: midibend
description: MIDI pitch bend: Sends a MIDI pitch bend message.

name: midichan
description: MIDI channel: Sets the MIDI channel for the event.

name: midicmd
description: MIDI command: Sends a MIDI command message.

name: midiport
description: MIDI port: Sets the MIDI port for the event.

name: miditouch
description: MIDI key after touch: Sends a MIDI key after touch message.

name: mockSoundMap
description:
Validates: Requirements 1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4
Bug Condition Exploration Test - Mini-notation Context and Case Sensitivity
This test encodes the EXPECTED (correct) behavior for bankHandler:

Suggestions should appear when typing inside mini-notation syntax within .bank()
Suggestions should use case-insensitive filtering
Suggestions should be returned in lowercase to match actual sound file names

On UNFIXED code, these tests are EXPECTED TO FAIL because:

bankCompletions() returns original casing (e.g., "RolandTR909") not lowercase
MiniNotationContextParser is NOT integrated into bankHandler

name: morph
description:
Takes two binary rhythms represented as lists of 1s and 0s, and a number
between 0 and 1 that morphs between them. The two lists should contain the same
number of true values.

name: mousex
description: The mouse's x position value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: mousey
description: The mouse's y position value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: mul
description: Multiplies each number by the given factor.

name: n
description:
Selects the given index from the sample map.
Numbers too high will wrap around.
n can also be used to play midi numbers, but it is recommended to use note instead.

name: never
description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0, fn) (never calls fn)

name: noise
description: Adds pink noise to the mix

name: note
description:
Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of

a letter (a-g or A-G)
optional accidentals (b or #)
optional (possibly negative) octave number (0-9). Defaults to 3

Examples of valid note names: c, bb, Bb, f#, c3, A4, Eb2, c#5
You can also use midi numbers instead of note names, where 69 is mapped to A4 440Hz in 12EDO.

name: nrpnn
description: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter number message.

name: nrpv
description: MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value: Sends a MIDI NRPN non-registered parameter value message.

name: octave
description: Sets the default octave of a synth.

name: off
description: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

name: often
description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.75, fn)

name: onsetsOnly
description:
Returns a new pattern, with all haps without onsets filtered out. A hap
with an onset is one with a whole timespan that begins at the same time
as its part timespan.

name: onTriggerTime
description:
make something happen on event time
uses browser timeout which is innacurate for audio tasks

name: orbit
description: An orbit is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

name: outside
description: Carries out an operation 'outside' a cycle.

name: pace
description:
Experimental
Speeds a pattern up or down, to fit to the given number of steps per cycle.
examples:
sound("bd sd cp").pace(4)
// The same as sound("{bd sd cp}%4") or sound("<bd sd cp>*4")

name: palindrome
description: Applies rev to a pattern every other cycle, so that the pattern alternates between forwards and backwards.

name: pan
description: Sets position in stereo.

params.name: pan
params.description: between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)

examples: s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))

name: panchor
description:
Sets the range anchor of the envelope:

anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv]
anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note]
If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

name: parseContext
description: Parse string context to find current pattern element

params.name: cursorOffset
params.description: Cursor position relative to string start

name: pattack
description: Attack time of pitch envelope.

name: Pattern
description: Create a pattern. As an end user, you will most likely not create a Pattern directly.

params.name: query
params.description: The function that maps a State to an array of Hap.

name: pcurve
description: Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

name: pdecay
description: Decay time of pitch envelope.

name: penv
description:
Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope.
If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, pattack:.2 will be the default.

name: perlin
description: Generates a continuous pattern of perlin noise, in the range 0..1.

name: phaser
description: Phaser audio effect that approximates popular guitar pedals.

name: phasercenter
description: The center frequency of the phaser in HZ. Defaults to 1000

name: phaserdepth
description: The amount the signal is affected by the phaser effect. Defaults to 0.75

name: phasersweep
description: The frequency sweep range of the lfo for the phaser effect. Defaults to 2000

params.name: phasersweep
params.description: most useful values are between 0 and 4000

name: pianoroll
description:
Visualises a pattern as a scrolling 'pianoroll', displayed in the background of the editor. To show a pianoroll for all running patterns, use all(pianoroll). To have a pianoroll appear below
a pattern instead, prefix with _, e.g.: sound("bd sd")._pianoroll().

params.name: options
params.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: cycles
params.description: number of cycles to be displayed at the same time - defaults to 4

params.name: playhead
params.description: location of the active notes on the time axis - 0 to 1, defaults to 0.5

params.name: vertical
params.description: displays the roll vertically - 0 by default

params.name: labels
params.description: displays labels on individual notes (see the label function) - 0 by default

params.name: flipTime
params.description: reverse the direction of the roll - 0 by default

params.name: flipValues
params.description: reverse the relative location of notes on the value axis - 0 by default

params.name: overscan
params.description: lookup X cycles outside of the cycles window to display notes in advance - 1 by default

params.name: hideNegative
params.description: hide notes with negative time (before starting playing the pattern) - 0 by default

params.name: smear
params.description: notes leave a solid trace - 0 by default

params.name: fold
params.description: notes takes the full value axis width - 0 by default

params.name: active
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the active notes - defaults to #FFCA28

params.name: inactive
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the inactive notes - defaults to #7491D2

params.name: background
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the background - defaults to transparent

params.name: playheadColor
params.description: hexadecimal or CSS color of the line representing the play head - defaults to white

params.name: fill
params.description: notes are filled with color (otherwise only the label is displayed) - 0 by default

params.name: fillActive
params.description: active notes are filled with color - 0 by default

params.name: stroke
params.description: notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

params.name: strokeActive
params.description: active notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default

params.name: hideInactive
params.description: only active notes are shown - 0 by default

params.name: colorizeInactive
params.description: use note color for inactive notes - 1 by default

params.name: fontFamily
params.description: define the font used by notes labels - defaults to 'monospace'

params.name: minMidi
params.description: minimum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 10

params.name: maxMidi
params.description: maximum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 90

params.name: autorange
params.description: automatically calculate the minMidi and maxMidi parameters - 0 by default

name: pick
description:
Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name).
Similar to inhabit, but maintains the structure of the original patterns.
examples: note("<0 1 2!2 3>".pick(["g a", "e f", "f g f g" , "g c d"]))

name: pickF
description: pickF lets you use a pattern of numbers to pick which function to apply to another pattern.

params.name: funcs
params.description: the array of functions from which to pull

name: pickmod
description:
The same as pick, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.
For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the
second one.

name: pickmodF
description:
The same as pickF, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the functions list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

params.name: funcs
params.description: the array of functions from which to pull

name: pickmodOut
description:
The same as pickOut, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickmodReset
description:
The same as pickReset, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickmodRestart
description:
The same as pickRestart, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.

name: pickOut
description: Similar to pick, but it applies an outerJoin instead of an innerJoin.

name: pickReset
description: Similar to pick, but the choosen pattern is reset when its index is triggered.

name: pickRestart
description: Similar to pick, but the choosen pattern is restarted when its index is triggered.

name: pitchwheel
description: Renders a pitch circle to visualize frequencies within one octave

name: ply
description: The ply function repeats each event the given number of times.

name: plyForEach
description:
The plyForEach function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.
This version of ply uses the iteration index as an argument to the function, similar to echoWith.

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index

name: plyWith
description: The plyWith function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.\n

params.name: func
params.description: function to apply, given the pattern

name: polymeter
description:
Experimental
Aligns the steps of the patterns, creating polymeters. The patterns are repeated until they all fit the cycle. For example, in the below the first pattern is repeated twice, and the second is repeated three times, to fit the lowest common multiple of six steps.
examples:
// The same as note("{c eb g, c2 g2}%6")
polymeter("c eb g", "c2 g2").note()

name: postgain
description: Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

name: prelease
description: Release time of pitch envelope
examples:
note("<c eb g bb> ~")
.release(.5) // to hear the pitch release
.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")

name: preserveCursorPosition
description: Preserves cursor position after formatting

name: press
description: Syncopates a rhythm, by shifting each event halfway into its timespan.

name: pressBy
description:
Like press, but allows you to specify the amount by which each
event is shifted. pressBy(0.5) is the same as press, while
pressBy(1/3) shifts each event by a third of its timespan.

name: prettierExtension
description: Main prettier extension that can be enabled/disabled

name: prettierKeymap
description: Creates the prettier keymap extension

name: progNum
description: MIDI program number: Sends a MIDI program change message.

name: pure
description: A discrete value that repeats once per cycle.

name: pw
description: Controls the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: pwrate
description: Controls the lfo rate for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: pwsweep
description: Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: queryArc
description: Query haps inside the given time span.

name: radio
description: Displays a radio button widget to allow the user to cycle through multiple options
examples:
radio(0, 1, 2, 3) // cycles through 0, 1, 2, 3
radio("bd", "sd", "hh") // cycles through drum sounds

name: rand
description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between 0 and 1.

name: rand2
description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between -1 and 1

name: range
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1.
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.
Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

name: range2
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

name: rangex
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range,
following an exponential curve.

name: rarely
description: Shorthand for .sometimesBy(0.25, fn)

name: ratio
description:
Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":".
Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

name: ref
description: exposes a custom value at query time. basically allows mutating state without evaluation

name: register
description: Registers a new pattern method. The method is added to the Pattern class + the standalone function is returned from register.

params.name: name
params.description: name of the function, or an array of names to be used as synonyms

params.name: func
params.description: function with 1 or more params, where last is the current pattern

name: release
description: Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

name: removeUndefineds
description:
Returns a new pattern, with haps containing undefined values removed from
query results.

name: repeatCycles
description: Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

name: replicate
description:
Experimental
replicate is similar to fast in that it increases its density, but it also increases the step count
accordingly. So stepcat("a b".replicate(2), "c d") would be the same as "a b a b c d", whereas
stepcat("a b".fast(2), "c d") would be the same as "[a b] [a b] c d".
TODO: find out how this function differs from extend
examples:
stepcat(
  sound("bd bd - cp").replicate(2),
  sound("bd - sd -")
).pace(8)

name: reset
description: Resets the pattern to the start of the cycle for each onset of the reset pattern.

name: restart
description:
Restarts the pattern for each onset of the restart pattern.
While reset will only reset the current cycle, restart will start from cycle 0.

name: rev
description: Reverse all haps in a pattern

name: ribbon
description:
Loops the pattern inside an offset for cycles.
If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

params.name: offset
params.description: start point of loop in cycles

name: room
description:
Sets the level of reverb.
When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: roomdim
description:
Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomfade
description:
Reverb fade time (in seconds).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomlp
description:
Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomsize
description:
Sets the room size of the reverb, see room.
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: rootNotes
description: Maps the chords of the incoming pattern to root notes in the given octave.

name: round
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded
to the nearest integer.

name: run
description: A discrete pattern of numbers from 0 to n-1

name: s
description:
Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters
separated by ':'.

params.name: sound
params.description: The sound / pattern of sounds to pick

name: saw
description: A sawtooth signal between 0 and 1.

name: saw2
description: A sawtooth signal between -1 and 1 (like saw, but bipolar).

name: scale
description:
Turns numbers into notes in the scale (zero indexed) or quantizes notes to a scale.
When describing notes via numbers, note that negative numbers can be used to wrap backwards
in the scale as well as sharps or flats (but not both) to produce notes outside of the scale.
Also sets scale for other scale operations, like {@link Pattern#scaleTranspose}.
A scale consists of a root note (e.g. c4, c, f#, bb4) followed by semicolon (':') and then a scale type.
The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

name: scaleTranspose
description:
Transposes notes inside the scale by the number of steps.
Expected to be called on a Pattern which already has a {@link Pattern#scale}

params.name: offset
params.description: number of steps inside the scale

name: scope
description: Renders an oscilloscope for the time domain of the audio signal.

params.name: align
params.description: if 1, the scope will be aligned to the first zero crossing. defaults to 1

params.name: color
params.description: line color as hex or color name. defaults to white.

params.name: pos
params.description: y-position relative to screen height. 0 = top, 1 = bottom of screen

params.name: trigger
params.description: amplitude value that is used to align the scope. defaults to 0.

name: scramble
description:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to shuffle,
but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

name: scrub
description:
Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file
in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

name: segment
description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

name: seq
description: Like cat, but the items are crammed into one cycle.

name: seqPLoop
description:
Similarly to arrange, allows you to arrange multiple patterns together over multiple cycles.
Unlike arrange, you specify a start and stop time for each pattern rather than duration, which
means that patterns can overlap.

name: sequence
description: See fastcat

name: sequenceP
description: Takes a list of patterns, and returns a pattern of lists.

name: setContext
description: Returns a new pattern with the context field set to every hap set to the given value.

name: setcpm
description: Changes the global tempo to the given cycles per minute

name: shape
description:
(Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud.
Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve
second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

name: showFirstCycle
description: More human-readable version of the firstCycleValues accessor.

name: showLoadingIndicator
description: Shows a loading indicator for formatting operations

name: shrink
description:
Experimental
Progressively shrinks the pattern by 'n' steps until there's nothing left, or if a second value is given (using mininotation list syntax with :),
that number of times.
A positive number will progressively drop steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.

name: shuffle
description:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order.
Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

name: silence
description: Does absolutely nothing..

name: sine
description: A sine signal between 0 and 1.

name: sine2
description: A sine signal between -1 and 1 (like sine, but bipolar).

name: sinefold
description: Wavefolding distortion composed with sinusoid

name: slice
description:
Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers.
Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

name: slider
description: Displays a slider widget to allow the user manipulate a value

name: slow
description: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

name: slowcat
description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle.

name: slowcatPrime
description: Concatenation: combines a list of patterns, switching between them successively, one per cycle. Unlike slowcat, this version will skip cycles.

name: soft
description: Soft-clipping distortion

name: someCycles
description: Shorthand for .someCyclesBy(0.5, fn)

name: someCyclesBy
description:
Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis.
Similar to sometimesBy

name: sometimes
description: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

name: sometimesBy
description:
Randomly applies the given function by the given probability.
Similar to someCyclesBy

name: sortHapsByPart
description:
Returns a new pattern, which returns haps sorted in temporal order. Mainly
of use when comparing two patterns for equality, in tests.

name: source
description: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

name: spectrum
description: Renders a spectrum analyzer for the incoming audio signal.

name: speed
description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: speed
params.description: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

name: spiral
description: Displays a spiral visual.

params.name: options
params.description: Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:

params.name: stretch
params.description: controls the rotations per cycle ratio, where 1 = 1 cycle / 360 degrees

params.name: cap
params.description: style of line ends: butt (default), round, square

params.name: inset
params.description: number of rotations before spiral starts (default 3)

params.name: playheadColor
params.description: color of playhead, defaults to white

params.name: playheadLength
params.description: length of playhead in rotations, defaults to 0.02

params.name: playheadThickness
params.description: thickness of playheadrotations, defaults to thickness

params.name: steady
params.description: steadyness of spiral vs playhead. 1 = spiral doesn't move, playhead does.

params.name: activeColor
params.description: color of active segment. defaults to foreground of theme

params.name: inactiveColor
params.description: color of inactive segments. defaults to gutterForeground of theme

params.name: colorizeInactive
params.description: wether or not to colorize inactive segments, defaults to 0

params.name: fade
params.description: wether or not past and future should fade out. defaults to 1

params.name: logSpiral
params.description: wether or not the spiral should be logarithmic. defaults to 0

name: splice
description: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

name: splitGluedAfterNumbers
description:
Puts a line break between a number and a statement glued to it ("175let x" -> "175\nlet x").
Only a run that starts with a digit outside an identifier is looked at, and it is split after the whole numeric
literal: 1e-4, 0x1f, 10n and identifiers like bass2hit or o0 stay intact (a digit-then-letter rule split
getTime() + 1e-4 into 1 and e-4, a syntax error).

name: splitQueries
description:
Returns a new pattern, with queries split at cycle boundaries. This makes
some calculations easier to express, as all haps are then constrained to
happen within a cycle.

name: spread
description: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

name: square
description: A square signal between 0 and 1.

name: square2
description: A square signal between -1 and 1 (like square, but bipolar).

name: squeeze
description:
Pick from the list of values (or patterns of values) via the index using the given
pattern of integers. The selected pattern will be compressed to fit the duration of the selecting event
examples: note(squeeze("<0@2 [1!2] 2>", ["g a", "f g f g" , "g a c d"]))

name: squiz
description:
Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as:
"A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

params.name: squiz
params.description: Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.

name: stack
description: The given items are played at the same time at the same length.

name: stepalt
description:
Experimental
Concatenates patterns stepwise, according to an inferred 'steps per cycle'.
Similar to stepcat, but if an argument is a list, the whole pattern will alternate between the elements in the list.
examples:
stepalt(["bd cp", "mt"], "bd").sound()
// The same as "bd cp bd mt bd".sound()

name: stepcat
description:
'Concatenates' patterns like fastcat, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle.
The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair.
Has the alias timecat.
examples:
stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()
// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()

name: stretch
description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

params.name: factor
params.description: inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.

name: striate
description: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

name: stripContext
description: Returns a new pattern with the context field of every hap set to an empty object.

name: struct
description: Applies the given structure to the pattern:
examples:
note("c,eb,g")
  .struct("x ~ x ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~ ~ x ~ x ~ ~")
  .slow(2)

name: stut
description: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

name: sub
description: Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.
examples:
n("0 2 4".sub("<0 1 2 3>")).scale("C4:minor")
// See add for more information.

name: superimpose
description: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

name: sustain
description: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

name: swing
description: Shorthand for swingBy with 1/3:

name: swingBy
description: The function swingBy x n breaks each cycle into n slices, and then delays events in the second half of each slice by the amount x, which is relative to the size of the (half) slice. So if x is 0 it does nothing, 0.5 delays for half the note duration, and 1 will wrap around to doing nothing again. The end result is a shuffle or swing-like rhythm

name: sysex
description: MIDI sysex: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

name: sysexdata
description: MIDI sysex data: Sends a MIDI sysex message.

name: sysexid
description: MIDI sysex ID: Sends a MIDI sysex identifier message.

name: tag
description: Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering. The function populates Hap.context.tags (Array).

name: take
description:
Experimental
Takes the given number of steps from a pattern (dropping the rest).
A positive number will take steps from the start of a pattern, and a negative number from the end.
examples:
"bd cp ht mt".take("2").sound()
// The same as "bd cp".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("1 2 3").sound()
// The same as "bd bd cp bd cp ht".sound()

"bd cp ht mt".take("-1 -2 -3").sound()
// The same as "mt ht mt cp ht mt".sound()

name: time
description: A signal representing the cycle time.

name: timecat
description: Aliases for stepcat

name: toBipolar
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 ..

Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the bipolar range -1 .. 1

name: toggle
description: Displays a toggle widget to allow the user switch between 0 and 1

name: tour
description:
Experimental
Inserts a pattern into a list of patterns. On the first repetition it will be inserted at the end of the list, then moved backwards through the list
on successive repetitions. The patterns are added together stepwise, with all repetitions taking place over a single cycle. Using pace to set the
number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
"[c g]".tour("e f", "e f g", "g f e c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

name: transpose
description:
Change the pitch of each value by the given amount. Expects numbers or note strings as values.
The amount can be given as a number of semitones or as a string in interval short notation.
If you don't care about enharmonic correctness, just use numbers. Otherwise, pass the interval of
the form: ST where S is the degree number and T the type of interval with

M = major
m = minor
P = perfect
A = augmented
d = diminished

Examples intervals:

1P = unison
3M = major third
3m = minor third
4P = perfect fourth
4A = augmented fourth
5P = perfect fifth
5d = diminished fifth

params.name: amount
params.description: Either number of semitones or interval string.

name: tremolo
description: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

name: tremolodepth
description: Depth of amplitude modulation

name: tremolophase
description: Alter the phase of the modulation waveform

params.name: offset
params.description: the offset in cycles of the modulation

name: tremoloshape
description: Shape of amplitude modulation
examples: note("{f g c d}%16").tremsync(4).tremoloshape("<sine tri square>").s("sawtooth")

name: tremoloskew
description: Alter the shape of the modulation waveform

params.name: amount
params.description: between 0 & 1, the shape of the waveform

name: tremolosync
description: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

name: tri
description: A triangle signal between 0 and 1.

name: tri2
description: A triangle signal between -1 and 1 (like tri, but bipolar).

name: undegrade
description:
Inverse of degrade: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for .undegradeBy(0.5)
Events that would be removed by degrade are let through by undegrade and vice versa (see second example).

name: undegradeBy
description:
Inverse of degradeBy: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount.
0 = 100% chance of removal
1 = 0% chance of removal
Events that would be removed by degradeBy are let through by undegradeBy and vice versa (see second example).

name: unison
description: Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")

name: unit
description: Used in conjunction with speed, accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using unit "c" means speed will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. speed "1" means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using unit "s" means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by speed.

name: validateSyntax
description: Validates JavaScript/TypeScript syntax

name: velocity
description: Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

name: vib
description: Applies a vibrato to the frequency of the oscillator.
examples:
// change the modulation depth with ":"
note("a e")
.vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>:12")
._scope()

name: vibmod
description: Sets the vibrato depth in semitones. Only has an effect if vibrato | vib | v is is also set
examples:
// change the vibrato frequency with ":"
note("a e")
.vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>:8")
._scope()

name: voicing
description:
Turns chord symbols into voicings. You can use the following control params:

chord: Note, followed by chord symbol, e.g. C Am G7 Bb^7
dict: voicing dictionary to use, falls back to default dictionary
anchor: the note that is used to align the chord
mode: how the voicing is aligned to the anchor

below: top note <= anchor
duck: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded
above: bottom note >= anchor


offset: whole number that shifts the voicing up or down to the next voicing
n: if set, the voicing is played like a scale. Overshooting numbers will be octaved

All of the above controls are optional, except chord.
If you pass a pattern of strings to voicing, they will be interpreted as chords.

name: voicings
description:
DEPRECATED: still works, but it is recommended you use .voicing instead (without s).
Turns chord symbols into voicings, using the smoothest voice leading possible.
Uses chord-voicings package.
examples: stack("<C^7 A7 Dm7 G7>".voicings('lefthand'), "<C3 A2 D3 G2>").note()

name: vowel
description: Formant filter to make things sound like vowels.

params.name: vowel
params.description: You can use a e i o u ae aa oe ue y uh un en an on, corresponding to [a] [e] [i] [o] [u] [æ] [ɑ] [ø] [y] [ɯ] [ʌ] [œ̃] [ɛ̃] [ɑ̃] [ɔ̃]. Aliases: aa = å = ɑ, oe = ø = ö, y = ı, ae = æ.

examples: s("bd sd mt ht bd [~ cp] ht lt").vowel("[a|e|i|o|u]")

name: warp
description: Amount of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator

params.name: amount
params.description: Warp of the wavetable from 0 to 1

name: warpattack
description: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpdc
description: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

params.name: dcoffset
params.description: dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar

name: warpdecay
description: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpdepth
description: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpenv
description: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: warpmode
description:
Type of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator.
The current options are: none, asym, bendp, bendm, bendmp, sync, quant, fold, pwm, orbit,
spin, chaos, primes, binary, brownian, reciprocal, wormhole, logistic, sigmoid, fractal, flip
examples:
s("morgana").bank("wt_digital").seg(8).note("F1").warp("0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1")
  .warpmode("<asym bendp spin logistic sync wormhole brownian>*2")

name: warprate
description: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warprelease
description: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpshape
description: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpskew
description: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

params.name: skew
params.description: How much to bend the LFO shape

name: warpsustain
description: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpsync
description: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable warp position

name: wchoose
description: Chooses randomly from the given list of elements by giving a probability to each element

name: wchooseCycles
description: Picks one of the elements at random each cycle by giving a probability to each element
examples: wchooseCycles(["bd bd bd",5], ["hh hh hh",3], ["sd sd sd",1]).fast(4).s()

// The probability can itself be a pattern
wchooseCycles(["bd(3,8)","<5 0>"], ["hh hh hh",3]).fast(4).s()

name: when
description: Applies the given function whenever the given pattern is in a true state.

name: whenKey
description:
Do something on a keypress, or array of keypresses
Key name reference

name: withContext
description: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the context field of every hap.

name: withHap
description: As with withHaps, but applies the function to every hap, rather than every list of haps.

name: withHaps
description: Returns a new pattern with the given function applied to the list of haps returned by every query.

name: withHapSpan
description:
Similar to withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to the timespans
of all haps returned by pattern queries (both part timespans, and where
present, whole timespans).

name: withHapTime
description:
As with withHapSpan, but the function is applied to both the
begin and end time of the hap timespans.

name: within
description: Use within to apply a function to only a part of a pattern.

params.name: end
params.description: end within cycle (0 - 1). Must be > start

params.name: func
params.description: function to be applied to the sub-pattern

name: withLoc
description:
Returns a new pattern with the given location information added to the
context of every hap.

name: withQuerySpan
description:
Returns a new pattern, where the given function is applied to the query
timespan before passing it to the original pattern.

name: withQueryTime
description:
As with withQuerySpan, but the function is applied to both the
begin and end time of the query timespan.

name: withValue
description:
Returns a new pattern, with the function applied to the value of
each hap. It has the alias fmap.

params.name: func
params.description: to to apply to the value

name: wordfall
description:
Displays a vertical pianoroll with event labels.
Supports all the same options as pianoroll.

name: wt
description: Position in the wavetable of the wavetable oscillator

params.name: position
params.description: Position in the wavetable from 0 to 1

name: wtattack
description: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtdc
description: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

params.name: dcoffset
params.description: dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar

name: wtdecay
description: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtdepth
description: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtenv
description: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtphaserand
description: Amount of randomness of the initial phase of the wavetable oscillator.

params.name: amount
params.description: Randomness of the initial phase. Between 0 (not random) and 1 (fully random)

name: wtrate
description: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtrelease
description: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtshape
description: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtskew
description: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

params.name: skew
params.description: How much to bend the LFO shape

name: wtsustain
description: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtsync
description: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: xfade
description:
Cross-fades between left and right from 0 to 1:

0 = (full left, no right)
.5 = (both equal)
1 = (no left, full right)

name: zip
description:
Experimental
'zips' together the steps of the provided patterns. This can create a long repetition, taking place over a single, dense cycle.
Using pace to set the number of steps per cycle is therefore usually recommended.
examples:
zip("e f", "e f g", "g [f e] a f4 c").note()
   .sound("folkharp")
   .pace(8)

name: zoom
description: Plays a portion of a pattern, specified by the beginning and end of a time span. The new resulting pattern is played over the time period of the original pattern:
examples:
s("bd*2 hh*3 [sd bd]*2 perc").zoom(0.25, 0.75)
// s("hh*3 [sd bd]*2") // equivalent
